current.text: Houston brought back Fred VanVleet and added Marcus Smart and Bogdan Bogdanovic, so the guard rotation is crowded.
The projected Houston starters are VanVleet, Amen Thompson, Kevin Durant, Jabari Smith Jr. and Alperen Sengun. Sheppard is not among them.
Ime Udoka blames him for defensive mistakes and pulls him quickly for them. Last season Udoka played Josh Okogie ahead of him.
Several experts think Udoka does not like him and will not change his mind.
Experts expect a smaller role than last season. Lloyd projects about 26 minutes and doubts he matches last season's minutes. Other experts see almost no path to a starting job without major injuries.
If he starts and plays about 28 to 30 minutes, he could be a top 40 to 50 player.
His ESPN rank of 58 is far too high. Lloyd doubts he breaks the top 100 and calls him his biggest fade on ESPN.
Draft him only as a cheap upside flyer. Josh values him at 1 USD. Lloyd is fine with him as a round-10 pick around 110 to 120.
Last season he ranked 93rd in head-to-head value. He was 129th before the trade deadline and 45th after it.
His season-total nine-category rank near 30th last season is misleading. It is high only because he played all 82 games.
With our March 28 end date, Houston plays 3, 3 and 4 games in fantasy playoff weeks 19 to 21. That is 10 games, a weak schedule.

durable.text: His category profile is strong for a guard: many threes, high steals and blocks, and good free throw shooting on low volume.
He is small and struggles on defense. He picks up his dribble too often and is too soft with the ball.
He is worth more in category leagues than in points leagues.
Udoka is a defense-first coach. He gives little room for error to poor defenders and plays his starters heavy minutes.

note: ESPN prices him at 8 USD (rank 58), but Yahoo has him at 1 USD (rank 149), and the experts agree with Yahoo. He went for 4 USD in our league last year, so keep him at 1 to 3 USD as a last-round flyer. He gives threes (+1.1 z vs guards), steals (+1.3) and blocks (+1.4) with no weak category, so he fits any build. His 43.6% FG is a mild drag, though. In the first weeks, check whether he gets 26 or more minutes or moves into the starting lineup after an injury. If he stays a short-minute bench guard behind VanVleet and Smart, drop him, because Houston's 10-game playoff schedule gives little reason to hold him.
